pageCache.text:
Welcome to Lakeside Primary School
It is a place we are all incredibly PROUD of - where children are safe, happy and flourish academically.
We are committed to ensuring our children experience the best education possible whilst we build positive working relationships with parents and carers.
Society today provides more opportunities and challenges than ever before. At Lakeside, we aim to prepare our children for these opportunities and challenges in order for them to achieve their personal potential.
You are warmly invited to discover more about our school by exploring this website...
Our Curriculum
Our curriculum, put simply, is all that we want a Lakeside pupil to learn over their time with us. It is designed to support every child in unlocking their potential, whether that is as the next budding scientist looking to make a great discovery, as a gifted athlete looking to stretch their personal best, or simply as someone who wants to enjoy developing a broad and exciting foundation of knowledge on which they can experience future successes.
Click on the button below to learn more about our Curriculum Tree, our three core questions, a subject-by-subject guide and much more....
We are Proud
Polite, well-mannered and respectful
Resilient and willing to learn from mistakes
Open-minded to new ideas and new ways of working
Understanding and accepting of others
Determined to be the best they can be

pageCache.text:
Our Vision and PROUD Values
The Lakeside vision exists to provide a clear and simple statement capturing what it is our school aspires to achieve. It is our ‘why’ - the reason staff get out of bed every morning to work with Lakeside pupils; the reason parents and carers bring their children through the gates each morning. It is designed to ensure every single child makes progress and enjoys success. The vision statement was crafted throughout the 2023-24 academic year with input from governors, leaders, staff and the parent/carer community.
Underpinning our vision sit an incredibly strong and embedded set of school values. These are the foundation upon which every child can build a successful school day, school week, school year and even school career. Values provide pupils with a sense of what is right and what is wrong and they can absolutely help shape a person’s mindset and behaviours over a lifetime.
Our values underpin all elements of life in our school. Children are celebrated for demonstrating our values and, over time, they become intrinsic motivators for all children to achieve their very best. All stakeholders—including staff—are expected to uphold our values and model them on a daily basis.
The values themselves are centred on the word PROUD. For us to be the most successful school we can be, we want to support everyone connected with the Lakeside community to be proud of themselves, proud of the school and proud of the community they are part of.
The children at Lakeside talk daily about the importance of their values—they encourage each other to demonstrate them and even hold one another to account for them. We strongly believe that by embedding these core values in the pupils of Lakeside, we are helping create children who are not just ready to learn in the here and now, but young people who will go on to become successful, well-rounded adults.

Thrive & Pastoral Care
For any child to achieve their full potential, they first need to feel grounded in a sense of safety and happiness. The Thrive Approach is used at Lakeside to focus upon children's emotional well-being. It offers practical strategies and skills that are built around assessments which identify children’s emotional development. Our qualified and highly experienced Thrive practitioners provide action plans for individual, small group and whole class needs. The sessions may take the form of small groups and one to one opportunities.

pageCache.pageTitle: Lakeside Primary School - Peripatetic Music at Lakeside
pageCache.text:
Peripatetic Music at Lakeside
We offer a range of peripatetic music lessons at Lakeside through external providers. These are offered through a private arrangement with the music teachers and hosted at school throughout the school day. The information below offers further information and contact details for the offer we have available at school:
Simon Probert Piano
The benefits of learning to play a musical instrument are many and varied. Making music opens children’s minds, and their confidence flourishes as they learn to express themselves in exciting new ways.
Most importantly though, making music is great fun and that will always be the best reason for learning! Our piano teacher, Simon Probert, has been giving weekly one-to-one lessons at Lakeside since 2021.
Where eligible, lessons can be subsidized using Pupil Premium funding. If you would like to find out more, or to register your child’s interest, please contact Simon by telephone (07720 400215) or email (simon@piano-lessons.co.uk).
Sarah Kelly Ukulele
Nick Powell Guitar
iRock
At iRock School of Music, we believe every child deserves a brighter future. Our in-school rock and pop band lessons provide an amazing confidence boosting experience for children by making music fun! 30-minute weekly lessons run like most other peripatetic classes. Children are grouped by age and learn together in their own rock bands. Children choose to become a drummer, guitarist, keyboard player or singer. We host regular 'rock concerts' in school for the children to show case their learning to friends and family.

pageCache.pageTitle: Lakeside Primary School - Smartphone Free at KS1, 2 & 3
pageCache.text:
Smartphone Free at KS1, 2 & 3
Lakeside Primary School is working in partnership with other local primary and secondary schools, as well as our parent communities, to encourage the delayed use of smartphones. We are committed to 'Smartphone Free at KS1, 2 and 3' to help us achieve our goal.
Why Smartphone Free?
A series of conversations with parents and professionals over the last few years have led us to this point. Collectively, our community has seen an increase in the number of concerning behaviour and safeguarding incidents related to primary age children passively using technology and having access to smart devices and social media apps. Parents tell us that they'd like to hold off giving their child a smartphone but, because everybody is doing it, it really is difficult to say no.
Simultaneously, we have seen a growing increase in local, national and international research around the dangers of children engaging with smartphones too young. Some of the statistics are, frankly, quite frightening. As well as this, we feel it is time to address some of the false-information leading to parents feeling a need to get their child a smartphone.
Our parent/carer survey in the spring of 2025 saw 80% of our community support the school in becoming a smartphone free environment.
September 2025 - The Smartphone Free at KS1, 2 & 3 Event
On the 23rd September 2025, Bournside School hosted an event for parents, carers and education professionals to hear from guest speakers from PAPAYA, Smartphone Free Childhood and the University of the West of England. The messages were powerful - check out the slides and read through the statistics here.
September 2025 - A United Response
At the beginning of the 2025-26 academic year, 15 local primary schools came together to share a united letter promoting a play-based childhood over a technology-based childhood. You can read the letter here.

Supporting Pupils with Disadvantage and SEND
At Lakeside, we believe that all pupils should have equitable access to our curriculum. Where pupils are disadvantaged or have SEND, we strive to remove the barriers that may limit this access. Within each year group curriculum overview, provision is mapped out through subjects and themes, ensuring full coverage of the National Curriculum at the same time as making meaningful and relevant links across broader themes and topics.
For pupils in receipt of the Pupil Premium Grant, we endeavour to meet costs that might otherwise prevent full access – for further information about provision through the Pupil Premium Grant, please see our Pupil Premium Strategy Statement on the website.
For pupils who have SEND, their My Plan, My Plan+ or EHCP will include outcomes that seek to remove barriers in accessing the curriculum – you will find further information about our SEND offer and policy on the website.
Mr S Timpson and Ms C Black lead Pupil Premium and SEND provision respectively. Please contact the admin team to arrange a meeting if you have any further queries: admin@lakeside.gloucs.sch.uk

At Lakeside our aim is for all children to leave us with the right tools and skills ready to start their new phase of learning in secondary school. In addition, we endeavour to instil a love of reading and writing in our children which will stay with them through all phases of their lives. We do this by following the National Curriculum (NC) for English – speaking and listening, reading and writing - through a creative approach which is underpinned by experiences and purpose.
For skills progression in reading and writing from Y1 – Y6 we follow the National Curriculum. We teach writing skills as specified by the National Curriculum and follow the guidelines for age related content. Our outcomes for writing are purpose-led, linked to themes and are framed by four key principles: to entertain, to inform, to discuss and to persuade, and spelling and grammar skills are threaded through following our own year group-specific programmes of study.

Subject Leaders - Mr Thomas and Miss Warren
At Lakeside Primary School, it is our intention to provide a high quality science education that recognises the importance of Science in every aspect of daily life. Our curriculum will enable children to become enquiry based learners, ask questions about the world around them and work scientifically to further their conceptual understanding and scientific knowledge. Children will be immersed in key scientific vocabulary, which develops their scientific knowledge and understanding. So much of science lends itself to outdoor learning and so we provide children with opportunities to experience this, through hands on experiences. We want the children to feel the ‘wow factor’ of science through immersing themselves and understanding how and why things work. Lakeside’s Science curriculum links directly to scientific knowledge, skills and understanding to ensure that learning is progressive and continuous.

Maths
The National Curriculum for Maths Key Stage 1 and Key Stage 2
The Lakeside Primary School 3Is for Maths

The Lakeside Can Do Maths Key Performance Indicators (including EYFS)
The Lakeside Can Do Maths + - x ÷ Calculation Progression Document
The Lakeside 2024 Maths Curriculum Evening Slides
Our aim is to enable all of our pupils to function as competent mathematicians in the real world as well as to develop awe and a love of maths. To learn why you need maths in everyday life gives the pupils a purpose to their learning.
Pupils learn to calculate using a range of methods through explaining their thinking. The use of mathematical vocabulary is encouraged in all lessons. The children have plenty of opportunities to develop their reasoning and logic through the use of problem solving and application of maths in their theme work.
Where possible the children apply their skills to help embed learning. Emphasis is placed on promoting the use of mathematical language to ensure that all pupils can explain mathematical processes effectively. Mastering skills and then applying them at depth underpins our mathematical curriculum.
It is vital that the children know their number bonds, number pairs and times table/division facts. These are taught at school but practising them at home helps the children to have a speedy recall of facts. We use the commutative law (if you know 6 x 3 = 18 then you know that 3 x 6 = 18) – see Kenny’s Pouch for the facts which need to be learned.

Modern Foreign Languages
The National Curriculum for MFL Key Stage 2
Click here for our Lakeside MFL Progression Document
French is our main modern foreign language with teaching beginning in Year 3.
French is taught through stories, songs, poems, rhymes and paintings following the objectives of the National Curriculum KS2 languages programme of study.
Each lesson builds on high-frequency grammatical structures learned in the previous lessons. Lessons provide opportunities for speaking and listening, with writing and some reading where relevant. Lessons are interactive and French is spoken as much as possible.

pageCache.pageTitle: Lakeside Primary School - School Opening Hours
pageCache.text:
School Opening Hours
Pedestrian gates to school are open to the parent community between 8:30am and 8:35am each day, from which time children should be dropped off at the classrooms. Morning registration to signal the start of the school day is at 8:45am, at which point the school bell rings and the gates are closed.
Lunch time at Lakeside is between 12pm and 1pm, with the afternoon registration period between 1pm and 1:05pm.
Between 3:05pm and 3:10pm the pedestrian gates will be open to the parent community for pick-up. The school bell rings to signal the end of the day at 3:15pm at which point children re-join their parents/carers.
The Lakeside school day is typically 6.5 hours long; the Lakeside school week is typically 32.5 hours long.
